pr_title: Rework the way USB core stack handles USB Interface Requests. (+reword)
pr_body:
Rework the way how the interfaces are handled by the USB core stack.
Until now USB stack was aware of only the first interface associated
with each class. This led to a problem when not first interface was
addressed by the request.

The usb_cfg_data struct is legacy of initial implementation
of USB device stack. It was implemented to support single function
devices with no composite support. The usb_cfg_data struct was
intended to be used to configure the device by calling
usb_set_config(). Because of how things grow this structure
was used to represent the USB functions rather than USB devices.

This patch:
 - allow to filter out the request at core level.
 - removes device configuration descriptor pointer.
   Adds pointer to list of pointers to USB interface descriptors
   associated with the function it represents.
 - renames some usb_cfg_data structure fields:
    interface -> request_handlers
	Name interface was used here as a communication interface
	between USB core stack and Class implementations.
	This naming could be missleading as USB specification defines
	interface as a part of the USB device descriptor.
    endpoint -> endpoints
	This change was made to reflect that there might be more than one
	endpoint. Additionaly it makes it consistent with newly added
	'interfaces' field.

Fixes: #24200 (USB3CV Chapter 9 tests for ECM)
pr_comments: I do not insist on last commit which rename things but I think this should be done as well.

**All checks passed.**

I named it wrongly. It's not a hack but it makes exception for just one thing. I wish we go in direction of making the stack more compact instead of creating an exception for just one type of request. Imo using `custom_handler` for "problematic" requests is acceptable. The solution proposed is fixing an issue we currently have and is presenting the approach of how to deal with such problems. I am thinking of another way to do that so `custom_handler` will not be required at all but its something I need to rethink.

issue_context.title: USB GET_INTERFACE response always 0, even when an alternate setting is used
comments:
First of all, whats the use case to add alternate setting for such device?
In order to make it work i suppose that [custom_handler](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/class/loopback.c#L169) must be implemented but I might be wrong as I took only i brief look into this. I cannot say when I will have time to do it as I am a bit busy right now and I do not see clear use case for that right now.
The current code is indeed incorrect but for all the classes and functionalities we support just right now its sufficient. 
Alternate settings are commonly used in audio class. Implementation could be found here #21526.
I think it would be worthwhile to implement it in audio for sure and as an author I will keep that in mind as for now it is missing.

Sorry for being a bit unclear - the example was just the quickest way I could find to create a patch that would fail in the USB compliance test. I'm tinkering with audio stuff and it was in that context that the issue was found. 

I can create a PR for a more generic solution; store the alternate setting after a successful USB SET_INTERFACE and returning that in the GET_INTERFACE request.
Ah, okay now I get this. If You want to post a PR it would be great. One question as You said 'generic solution'. Where do You gonna store the info about alternate setting?
Good question. If zephyr only supports one interface would it be out of place to store it in struct usb_dev_priv?

Until now it supported no alternate settings but many interfaces. For example if You configure 2x cdc there will be 4 interfaces in total. 

It cant be in usb_dev_priv as on this level You are not possible to guess the total number of interfaces so there is no possibility to create a table or whatsoever to store this information.
I think the only way now is to implement [custom_handler](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/include/usb/usb_device.h#L161) as it is called prio the [std_interface_req()](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/usb_device.c#L914), but this will get tricky as well because of how the set_interface is handled..
We can follow up on Slack, feel free to ping me there.

review_comments: This is a change of the API. I guess it should be documented.
Why `-EINVAL`? Wasn't this request handled successfully?

Yes it was but, ekhmm its Zephyr. Let me explain why. We have recently introduced this behaviour in audio PR. `custom_handler` has its special [return type](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/include/usb/usb_device.h#L160). This is done like that because class implementation handles the status of alternate interface and for set/get request it saves/returns the number of alternate that was requested. For SET however one more thing needs to be done -> proper endpoints associated with that alternate must be enabled or disabled.

Class custom handler is called from [there](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/usb_device.c#L915). Look closely at this if condition. If I `return 0` there it will return from `usb_handle_standard_request` without calling `usb_handle_std_interface_req` which enabled/disables the associated endpoints.

Reference: [audio](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/subsys/usb/class/audio/audio.c#L736).
A comment like "This request needs further processing in the core USB stack, hence -EINVAL is returned." would be helpful then. In the audio case, too.
I will add this as a separate commit.

This behavior is confusing, we have to rework it somehow asap. What about not to do it in custom_handler but implement a specific handler to set interface which would be called from REQ_SET_INTERFACE(usb_set_interface)?

In commit `usb: ECM fix to pass USB3CV tests`
Could we just say `Fixes #24200` instead of the longer string.
That is something to discus, I think it has to be handled here and we have to store "currently selected alternate setting" in the `struct usb_cfg_data`.

Typo in commit msg `usb: Rework the usb core internals.`
